# rwgpu 0.1.0 command line

Every command accepts `--json` and then prints exactly one JSON object on stdout with `rwgpu`, `format`, `command`, `ok`, `errors`, `warnings` and `diagnostics` fields plus the command's own fields. Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` errors or failed checks, `2` bad command line.

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| [`rwgpu new PATH [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-new) | Create a project from the starter template |
| [`rwgpu check [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-check) | Validate every project file without running anything |
| [`rwgpu run [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-run) | Run a scene headless for N frames |
| [`rwgpu shot [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-shot) | Render a frame to PNG, with a text report of what is drawn where |
| [`rwgpu inspect [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-inspect) | Dump the world state at a frame as JSON (or a table) |
| [`rwgpu test [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-test) | Run playtests: scripted input, expectations and reference screenshots |
| [`rwgpu explain [TOPIC] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-explain) | Explain a diagnostic code, a file format/component, or a command |
| [`rwgpu schema [KIND] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-schema) | Print the JSON Schema of a file format |
| [`rwgpu docs [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-docs) | Print the reference docs for this exact rwgpu version |
| [`rwgpu serve [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-serve) | Serve the web player for a project (reloads when files change) |
| [`rwgpu help [COMMAND] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-help) | Show help for rwgpu or a command |
| [`rwgpu version [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-version) | Print the rwgpu version |

## rwgpu new

```text
rwgpu new — Create a project from the starter template

Usage: rwgpu new PATH [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  PATH         Folder to create (must not exist or be empty).

Flags:
  --name NAME        Project name (default: the folder name).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Writes rwgpu.toml, a starter scene, prefabs, a playtest and an AGENTS.md generated for this rwgpu version, then checks the result.

Examples:
  rwgpu new my-game
  rwgpu new games/maze --name "Maze"
```

## rwgpu check

```text
rwgpu check — Validate every project file without running anything

Usage: rwgpu check [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to rwgpu.toml.

Flags:
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Parses rwgpu.toml, every scene, prefab and playtest; checks types, unknown keys, references between files and static problems (overlapping solids, signals that can never fire). Exit code 1 if there are errors; warnings do not fail.

Examples:
  rwgpu check
  rwgpu check my-game --json
```

## rwgpu run

```text
rwgpu run — Run a scene headless for N frames

Usage: rwgpu run [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to rwgpu.toml.

Flags:
  --frames N         Frames (fixed steps) to run. Default: the playtest's frames, else 300.
  --input FILE       Drive the scene with a playtest's [[input]] (and use its scene and seed).
  --seed N           Override the random seed.
  --events           Include the event log.
  --hash-every N     Record the state hash every N frames (to find where two runs diverge).
  --track NAME       Print the cells an entity occupies, with frame ranges (timing puzzles, patrols).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Deterministic: the same files, input and seed always give the same state hash, on every platform. No window and no GPU are used.

Examples:
  rwgpu run --frames 300
  rwgpu run tests/walkthrough.toml --events
  rwgpu run --frames 120 --track guard
  rwgpu run scenes/garden.toml --input tests/walkthrough.toml --json
```

## rwgpu shot

```text
rwgpu shot — Render a frame to PNG, with a text report of what is drawn where

Usage: rwgpu shot [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to rwgpu.toml.

Flags:
  --frame N          Frame to render. Default: the playtest's last frame, else 0.
  --input FILE       Drive the scene with a playtest's [[input]] (and use its scene and seed).
  --seed N           Override the random seed.
  --out FILE         PNG path. Default: out/<scene>_f<frame>.png in the project.
  --compare FILE     Compare with a reference PNG; exit 1 if it differs (writes <out>.diff.png).
  --max-diff N       With --compare: pixels allowed to differ (default 0).
  --report           Print the frame report (always included with --json).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Rendering is a deterministic CPU rasterizer: identical pixels on every machine. The frame report lists each entity's screen rectangle, visible pixels and what covers it, and flags off-screen (W0301), hidden (W0302) and clipped (W0303) entities.

Examples:
  rwgpu shot
  rwgpu shot --input tests/walkthrough.toml --report
  rwgpu shot --frame 120 --out a.png --json
```

## rwgpu inspect

```text
rwgpu inspect — Dump the world state at a frame as JSON (or a table)

Usage: rwgpu inspect [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to rwgpu.toml.

Flags:
  --frame N          Frame to inspect. Default: the playtest's last frame, else 0.
  --input FILE       Drive the scene with a playtest's [[input]] (and use its scene and seed).
  --seed N           Override the random seed.
  --entity NAME      Only this entity (and, with --events, its events).
  --component NAME   Only entities with this component (sprite, trigger, ...).
  --events           Include the event log: what happened and what was refused, and why.
  --since N          With --events: only events from frame N on.
  --place PREFAB[@X,Y] Can I build here? With a cell: whether a `spawn` of PREFAB fits there at this frame, and why not. Without: every cell where it fits. Prints only that answer (add --entity for the table).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Answers what exists, where it is, and why something happened. The text table is a summary (cell, components, solid, cooldown, patrol target, screen rectangle, tap point); --json has every component and all runtime state, plus `ground` (size, and the map and terrain legend for terrain maps). `tap` is a pixel where a tap is guaranteed to hit the entity. `--place` applies the same rules as the `spawn` action (inside the ground, buildable terrain, nothing enabled standing there).

Examples:
  rwgpu inspect --json
  rwgpu inspect --input tests/walkthrough.toml --frame 60 --entity player --events
  rwgpu inspect --input tests/build.toml --frame 120 --place house@3,2
```

## rwgpu test

```text
rwgpu test — Run playtests: scripted input, expectations and reference screenshots

Usage: rwgpu test [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder or a single playtest file (default: current folder).

Flags:
  --filter TEXT      Only playtests whose name contains TEXT.
  --update-refs      Write reference images from the current output instead of comparing.
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Runs every tests/*.toml. Failed expectations are E0401 with the entity's recent events; image mismatches are E0402 and write the actual and diff images under out/tests/.

Examples:
  rwgpu test
  rwgpu test --filter walk --json
  rwgpu test --update-refs
```

## rwgpu explain

```text
rwgpu explain — Explain a diagnostic code, a file format/component, or a command

Usage: rwgpu explain [TOPIC] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [TOPIC]      A code (E0103), a component or format (sprite, entity, connect, playtest) or a command. Omit to list topics.

Flags:
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Like `rustc --explain`, for rwgpu's codes and file formats.

Examples:
  rwgpu explain
  rwgpu explain E0201
  rwgpu explain sprite
  rwgpu explain trigger --json
```

## rwgpu schema

```text
rwgpu schema — Print the JSON Schema of a file format

Usage: rwgpu schema [KIND] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [KIND]       project, scene, prefab or playtest. Omit to list them.

Flags:
  --out DIR          Write all schemas into DIR as <kind>.schema.json.
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Editors (e.g. VS Code + Even Better TOML) can use these for completion and inline errors.

Examples:
  rwgpu schema scene
  rwgpu schema --out .rwgpu/schema
```

## rwgpu docs

```text
rwgpu docs — Print the reference docs for this exact rwgpu version

Usage: rwgpu docs [FLAGS]

Flags:
  --agents           Print the AGENTS.md that `rwgpu new` writes into projects.
  --out DIR          Write cli.md, formats.md, errors.md and schemas/ into DIR.
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Docs are generated from the same registries the engine uses, so they always match the installed version.

Examples:
  rwgpu docs
  rwgpu docs --agents > AGENTS.md
```

## rwgpu serve

```text
rwgpu serve — Serve the web player for a project (reloads when files change)

Usage: rwgpu serve [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to rwgpu.toml.

Flags:
  --port N           Port on 127.0.0.1 (default 4410).
  --wasm FILE        Path to rwgpuengine_web.wasm (default: the workspace build, see `cargo xtask web`).

Opens nothing by itself; visit the printed URL. URL parameters: scene=PATH, input=PATH, frames=N (run N frames immediately, then pause). The page shows the frame number and state hash, which match `rwgpu run` for the same input.

Examples:
  rwgpu serve examples/iso_garden
  rwgpu serve --port 8080
```

## rwgpu help

```text
rwgpu help — Show help for rwgpu or a command

Usage: rwgpu help [COMMAND] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [COMMAND]    Command to describe.

Flags:
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

`rwgpu help --json` lists every command, argument and flag as data.

Examples:
  rwgpu help
  rwgpu help shot
  rwgpu help --json
```

rwgpu version — Print the rwgpu version

Examples:
